page.layout: One page of text in two columns of running text, the left column wider than the right; no margin notes beyond the marginal reference letters in the left margin. Running head at the top right. Page number at the top right. Line-ending letters in the left margin are fragments of text on the facing page and are not transcribed.

main_text.l: Inter alia ridicula ac fuperftitiofa quæ à Pontifi-
ciis mutuatur, hæc funt. Nam 1. Presbyteri tenentur
matutinas & vespertinas illas preces fingulis diebus publice
vel privatim prælegere, pag. libri illius. 7. Porro si
privatim & folus prælegat, quis ufus refponfio-
num per populum: nisi forte intelligendum sit, de-
bere presbyterum sibi respondere nomine ecclesiæ
quam repræfentat, & sic preces hæ cum sint publica
authoritate institutæ, & prolatæ à publica per-
sona, deputata ab ecclesia ad orandum nomine
suo, & hac intentione ut expleat munus suum,
quid aliud erunt quam preces illæ Papistarum pu-
blicæ, seu horæ Canonicæ, quarum duæ ex se-
ptem reponuntur. vide Bellarm. tom. 4. Contro-
vers. lib. 1. De bonis operibus in particulari. cap.
10. 2. Nullus certus locus destinatur matutinis &
vespertinis precibus publicis; sed remittitur arbi-
trio Episcopi, qui sedulo studebit templorum for-
mam ad tempora præcedentia revocare, hoc est,
quando Papismus regnabat, ad similitudinem fcil.
templi Salomonis, divisi in porticum, navim, &
sacrarium. 3. Quædam alta voce à presbytero proferen-
da sunt, alia vero voce submissa, quæ forma ponti-
ficiis confueta est in mysterio Missæ, preces etiam
quædam, confessio fidei, & alia jubentur legi aut
cani, cum tamen in metrum non redigantur.
4. licet situs corporis indifferens sit, in quibusdam
tamen precibus indicitur, ut genibus flexis prece-
mur; in aliis ut stemus; in aliis vero nullus om-
nino corporis situs imperatur; Et aliquando populus
jubetur orare non presbyter, & vice versa,
aliquando populus jubetur comprecari cum pres-
bytero, quandoque repetit, quandoque resp-
ondet, & alias orationem inter se dividunt, ju-
betur presbyter aliquando faciem ad populum
convertere, aliquando ergo avertit: stare
cum

page.notes: Marginal letters and fragments of the facing page at the left edge are not transcribed. Several words in the lower lines are slightly blurred; the final line ("cum") is a catchword-like continuation and is kept in the text. Printed text is in Latin with some long-s forms rendered as s; the fragment "s" was normalised. Some words in the text are doubtful and not individually marked.
